encoding_notes: SOURCE = TIER_B_blocked_shell. The live Springer guide is Akamai 'Client Challenge' bot-blocked to every fetch path tried (WebFetch->idp auth 303; Apify headless->Client Challenge; www.springer.com mirror identical) AND has never been captured by the Wayback Machine (zero snapshots), so no archive fallback exists. Journal-specific values below come from Google-indexed excerpts of that blocked live guide (surfaced via WebSearch, convergent across multiple independent queries) plus the reachable Paperpile CSL page for reference style. Per contract this is weaker than a direct render; caps are flagged by confidence.

word_limits.original_research (HIGH confidence — convergent across every query): Original Articles no more than 2,500 words, abstract 150 words (max 250 acceptable), no more than 5 figures and 3 tables, and a maximum of 40 references. This tight 2,500-word cap is a well-known distinctive IO rule.
word_limits.review (MEDIUM — single convergent snippet): 'Review Articles should have no more than 3,500 words and 100 references.' No stated review abstract/figure/table cap -> null.

word_limits.case_report (MEDIUM — single snippet): 'Case reports should not exceed 1500 words and should include 5 references.' The '5 references' is encoded as references_max=5 (ambiguous whether exactly-5 or up-to-5). No stated case-report abstract/figure/table cap -> null.

blinding.double_blind = true: 'The journal follows a double-blind reviewing procedure' — the author remains anonymous to reviewers throughout peer review. separate_title_page = true: 'A separate Title Page should be submitted, containing title, author names, affiliations, and the contact information of the corresponding author.' scrub_body_identifiers = true (implied by double-blind: identifying info must be kept out of the main manuscript file). scrub_metadata = false (document/file metadata scrub not mentioned).

title_page.elements from the separate-title-page sentence above: article_title, authors, affiliations, corresponding_author. title_max_chars = 250: 'The title should be short and descriptive, and less than 250 characters in length (including spaces)' (single clear quoted sentence; MEDIUM confidence). running_title_max_chars, title_max_words, authors_degrees all unstated -> null.

abstract.structured = true, max_words = 250: 'A structured abstract of 150 to 250 words should be divided into sections including Purpose...' Only the opening label 'Purpose' is directly evidenced; sections encoded as Purpose/Methods/Results/Conclusion = IO's standard structured-abstract set (the distinctive non-standard 'Purpose' opener is the IO signature) — Methods/Results/Conclusion are the standard completion, MEDIUM confidence. max_words = 250 is the abstract ceiling (target 150).

abstract.keywords.required = false + all null: IO very likely requires keywords (Springer norm), but the reachable excerpts gave no reliable keyword count (one snippet's '4 to 6' was summarizer-hedged and unreliable) — kept conservative/unstated rather than fabricate.

sections.original_research from: 'the text should be divided into Introduction, Materials and Methods, Results, Discussion, Acknowledgements, Conflict of Interest, and References.' Encoded the core IMRaD+References order; Acknowledgements/Conflict-of-Interest and the other declaration blocks are carried in the declarations object instead. No explicit section order was found for review or case_report -> omitted from the sections map.

references.style = custom (Springer 'Basic' style): reference entries format as 'Author AA, Author BB (Year) Title. Journal-abbrev Vol:pages' (year in parentheses after authors) — matches neither vancouver/nlm/ama cleanly (Paperpile example: 'Karlseder J, Smogorzewska A, de Lange T (2002) Senescence induced by altered telomere state, not telomere loss. Science 295:2446-2449'). in_text = bracket: Paperpile 'References should be cited in the text by sequential numbers in square brackets' with examples [1], [1, 2], [1-4]. order = cited (sequential numbering by appearance). journal_abbrev = nlm ('Int. Orthop.' abbreviated). include_doi = false: Paperpile explicitly says the guide does not mention DOI inclusion, and its example carries no DOI — set conservative false rather than infer from Springer house style. et_al_threshold null (Paperpile example lists all 4 authors; no explicit threshold stated). max_count null (per-type ref caps live in word_limits).

declarations from: 'Manuscripts must include the following sections between the Discussion (Conclusion) and References: Funding, Conflicts of interest, Data availability statement, Author contribution statement, and Ethics approval.' -> required = funding, conflict_of_interest, data_availability, author_contributions, ethics_approval. order adds acknowledgments at the front (it appears in the body-section list, before the declaration block). patient_consent is NOT in the explicit declaration list but IO requires informed consent for human studies / consent for publication for case reports (per the SICOT ethics statement) — omitted from required to stay evidence-based.

FORCED-ENUM defaults (schema has no null slot) chosen as least-transforming because the live guide is blocked and these were not evidenced: layout.line_numbers = 'none' (line-numbering requirement UNVERIFIED — a double-blind journal may well require continuous line numbers, but no reachable source confirms it); tables.placement = 'in_text'; figures.legends_location = 'in_text'. Treat all three as unverified.

UNVERIFIED / null due to blocked guide (no reachable evidence): page_size, font family/size, line_spacing, margins, alignment, first_line_indent, page_numbers, running_head, headings; figures.separate_files (set conservative false though Springer norm is separate files), figures.formats ([]), figures.min_dpi, callout_style, naming_pattern; tables caption_position + numbering; misc.orcid_required (false conservative), cover_letter_required (false — IO's current Editorial Manager system collects statements in-interface, no cover-letter requirement evidenced), highlights_required (null), title_case (null).

identity.issn = null: IO is widely published as ISSN 0341-2695 (print) / 1432-5195 (electronic), but this was NOT confirmed from a reachable source this session and the contract forbids filling from training memory — left null. submission_system = Editorial Manager (www.editorialmanager.com/inor), confirmed by the SICOT.org journal page and multiple snippets.

article_types mapping: 'Original Article' -> original_research; 'Review Article' -> review; 'Case Report' -> case_report. IO likely also accepts editorials/letters/current-concepts, but no reachable evidence delimited them, so only the three evidenced author-submittable types are encoded.

SCHEMA GAPS: (1) IO's dual abstract length (target 150 / ceiling 250) is collapsed to a single max_words=250. (2) Compliance note from the guide — 'Articles not compliant with the submission instructions will be immediately sent back to the author' — has no schema slot. (3) File-format requirement (.docx/.doc, Word 2007+) has no schema slot. (4) 'Use the table function, not spreadsheets, to make tables' has no schema slot.
